svg.title: Nuclear Power and New Trees
svg.desc: A proposal for 100 gigawatts of new nuclear power and a forest fund of up to 220 million dollars a year. Calculated nuclear output is 798 terawatt-hours per year. Forest scenario funds about 59,000 hectares in one planting cohort. Construction costs 600 billion to 1 trillion dollars before financing and other costs. Replace solar only when replacement power is ready. Click to read the full proposal.

g.text: WALTER MCDONALD · ECON 238 · WEEK ELEVEN
Nuclear Power and New Trees
Build reactors at suitable sites. Put real funding into forests.
100 GW added by 2050
798 TWh / year
At the 2025 nuclear capacity factor of 91.1%.
About 18% of 2025 U.S. utility-scale generation.
$600 billion-$1 trillion in overnight capital.
Older DOE benchmark; financing and other costs extra.
Up to $220 million / year
59,000 hectares
One funded cohort, after a 20% support reserve.
Assumes $3,000 per hectare. No land purchases.
Funding needs congressional approval.
Private solar-company research money is not public cash.
Replacement first.
Blocking 10 GW of solar for 7 years could add 65 million tons CO2e if gas fills the gap.
Illustrative life-cycle comparison. Keep useful solar until a better replacement is ready.
Sources: EIA, DOE, NREL, Fargione et al.
Scenarios, not forecasts. Full sources and limits in the proposal.
Nuclear construction has separate financing. Forest benefits require survival, care and time.
